title: Basic web performance and accessibility audit
learningObjectives: Complete basic web performance and accessibility audit using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: A basic audit measures loading and interaction performance and reviews semantic structure, keyboard operation, focus visibility, contrast, reflow, and accessible names. Use browser tools and automated scanners as aids, then complete manual checks.
understand.whyItMatters: Performance and accessibility are product qualities, not final decorations. A simple audit identifies high-impact fixes before publication.
understand.analogy: An audit is a final inspection of both the speed and usability of the finished route.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The checklist covers representative audit dimensions. Record actual measurements and observed issues for the project.

examples.explanation: The checklist covers representative audit dimensions. Record actual measurements and observed issues for the project.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Run a performance recording and accessibility scan, then manually test keyboard and zoom. Prioritise issues by user impact.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
